recomputed: All 42 SOURCES.tsv entries matched their SHA-256 and byte size (26,442,501 bytes), as did all 12 registered or repository inputs. Checked the contents of each file, including PDF pages, Office archives and their sheets or figures, versioned HTML, GEO gzip streams, and repository inventories. The four PMC supplements match the publisher copies byte for byte. Read the three current review records, verified the absence of a dataset entry in additional-comparison-specs and concordance-reviews, and checked the registry and existing combined S1 comparator. Preprint v1 reports 10,359 at adjusted P < 0.05 out of a stated 28,226 protein-coding genes. Versions 2 and 3 and the published paper give 1,407. GEO has 54,532 unique Ensembl IDs by 20 libraries, zero sample supplements and nine acute libraries (GSM7469357–61 control, GSM7469362–65 Gly-Low). Applying the registered symbol aggregation and expression filter to the acute counts reproduces 17,169 tested rows, including 152 unmapped, and exactly the 17,017 published symbols. The DE table and Explorer track both give 10,146 FDR < 0.05 calls. Using the full-precision DE table, S1 3A/B gives 32/32 matched signs, Pearson 0.99856498, Spearman 0.98900293 and median absolute log2 difference 0.01374432. S2 S4F gives 113/113, 0.99999562, 0.99975048 and 0.01923283, with zero author adjusted P values. S2 S4E gives 2/2 matched signs and median absolute difference 0.15877070. Preprint v2 S4A gives 4/5 paired, 4/4 signs, one shared positive (Gh), two local-only (Ghsr and Ghrh), zero author-only among finite pairs and one in neither (Ghr). Of 10,146 local positives, 10,143 lack a usable preprint-panel adjusted P. Ghrhr has author adjusted P 0.0342 and no local test. For all 128 S1 sample ratios, Pearson is 0.99999344 and maximum absolute log2 difference is 0.03849136 using the two registered Eno1 features. Verified all eight computed claims, identifier mappings and denominators. The combined S1 reference and S4F each meet both numerical routes within selected genes. The 1,407-gene membership and generating rule remain unresolved, which supports needs_author_contact. The correction retains existing ledger enums and no signed-off contrast.
problems: The proposal attributes the five-control/four-treated library count to the RNA-seq Methods as well as GEO and implies that cohort size applies across panels. The Methods specify age and treatment duration. GEO and the sample sheet establish library counts. The published Figure S4E legend explicitly gives four mice per group. Its significance marks give figure-test bounds for Fcf1 and Nip7, and the identities of the controls underlying that panel are unclear.

The criteria say ‘per panel,’ although the existing Table S1 reference combines 20 Figure 3A and 12 Figure 3B genes. The 32-gene reference reaches the policy minimum only in combination. All 113 rows of S4F form a separate reference. Its Speakman/Gly-Low correlation of -0.62631251 also identifies the corresponding preprint v3 Figure S4E plot despite the different published panel letters.

The summary implies a change in the selection rule and a complete lack of information on gene identities. The sources establish a change in the reported total. They name selected genes, and preprint v2 Figure 4C reports 711 upregulated genes. They do not supply the full membership or establish why the total changed.

Ghrhr was recorded simply as having no published row. A replay of the registered expression filter identifies the reason. ENSMUSG00000004654 met the 0.45019129 CPM cutoff in three acute libraries. Four were required, so the comparison has no local adjusted P for this gene.
